title: FACET: Teacher-Centred LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems—Towards Personalized Educational Worksheets
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of how generative AI can support teachers in differentiating instruction for increasingly heterogeneous classrooms. The authors argue that many current AI personalization tools are student-facing and overly focused on performance, while neglecting motivational, emotional, and pedagogical dimensions that matter for classroom teaching.

To respond to this gap, the paper introduces FACET, a teacher-facing multi-agent LLM framework for generating individualized worksheets. The system uses three specialized agents: learner agents that simulate different student profiles, a teacher agent that adapts tasks according to didactical principles and Bloom’s taxonomy, and an evaluator agent that scores the output on didactical structure, clarity, creativity, and suitability for learner needs. The implementation is demonstrated with authentic grade 8 mathematics curriculum content from German secondary education.

The study evaluates the framework through automated agent-based scoring across ten iterations per learner profile and exploratory feedback from five K-12 in-service mathematics teachers. Results suggest that the generated worksheets were stable, well aligned to the learner profiles, and perceived by teachers as suitably differentiated, especially in structure and task appropriateness. The paper concludes that multi-agent LLM systems may offer a scalable pathway for teacher support in personalized material generation, but notes that stronger classroom-based validation and richer learner profiles are still needed.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based large language model family used here for learner-agent, teacher-agent, and evaluator-agent functions within a multi-agent system.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the underlying LLM for the FACET framework: GPT-4.1 for learner and teacher agents, and GPT-4o for evaluator and formatting, to generate personalized mathematics worksheets and automated quality feedback.

findings.finding_summary: The paper reports exploratory feasibility evidence that the ChatGPT-based multi-agent system could generate worksheets tailored to four learner profiles, with consistently high automated ratings across 10 iterations per profile. Agent-based evaluation found strong scores for suitability (M=4.78, SD=0.06) and clarity (M=4.76, SD=0.12), while teacher feedback from five K-12 in-service teachers also rated didactical structure and suitability positively.
findings.measure: Worksheet quality ratings from automated evaluator agent and exploratory teacher expert ratings (didactical structure, clarity, creativity, suitability)
findings.sample_size: n=10 iterations per profile; n=5 teachers

quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory mixed-methods feasibility study with automated agent ratings and small-scale teacher feedback, not a controlled efficacy trial. The evidence is useful but methodologically preliminary and limited in external validity.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported outcomes are positive but are descriptive ratings rather than a measured causal effect on teacher planning quality or student outcomes. No effect size is reported, so impact cannot be quantified beyond preliminary feasibility.
